messages:
Maya (Support): FYI customer ACME reporting DNS failures resolving their private service endpoint from prod VPC: `svc.acme.internal`. They see NXDOMAIN from app hosts. Repro steps they gave: `curl http://svc.acme.internal/health` -> curl: (6) Could not resolve host: svc.acme.internal

Maya (Support): Attached dig from a prod app host:```
$ dig svc.acme.internal @10.0.0.2 +short
;; -> (nothing)
;; status: NXDOMAIN
```

Maya (Support): Customer says staging resolves fine, only prod affected. No recent infra changes on their side. Can netops confirm split-horizon / hosted zone associations?

Hao (NetOps): Thanks — first checks: are the VPCs associated with the Route53 private hosted zone? Can you run: `aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id ZONEID` (replace) OR `aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --dnsname acme.internal` and paste VPC list. Also confirm VPC id in prod and which account the hosted zone lives in.

Maya (Support): Ran `aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id /hostedzone/ZHACME` from our ops account, output VPC list shows only `vpc-0abcd (us-west-2)` which matches their staging VPC. Prod VPC is `vpc-0f123` and is NOT in the VPC list.

Sam (Oncall): That would explain NXDOMAIN in prod — private hosted zone only associated with staging. Two quick checks: 1) make sure the hosted zone is private (not public) and name matches exactly (no trailing dot mismatch). 2) If hosted zone is in a different AWS account, you need to create an association authorization from the hosted-zone account before associating the other VPC.

Hao (NetOps): Commands:```
# from hosted-zone account
aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id ZHACME
# authorize prod account (if needed)
aws route53 create-vpc-association-authorization --hosted-zone-id ZHACME --vpc VPCRegion=us-west-2,VPCId=vpc-0f123
# then from prod account (or same)
aws route53 associate-vpc-with-hosted-zone --hosted-zone-id ZHACME --vpc VPCRegion=us-west-2,VPCId=vpc-0f123
```
Also check for any public hosted zone with same name that could cause confusing behavior: `aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --dnsname acme.internal`

Maya (Support): Tried `create-vpc-association-authorization` from hosted-zone account, got `AuthorizationAlreadyExists`? Hmm looked closer — hosted zone is actually owned by acme-ops account, we were running from our ops account. Route53 Bot just posted a note:

Route53 Bot: Reminder — cross-account assoc requires calling `create-vpc-association-authorization` from the hosted zone owner account. If you see `AuthorizationAlreadyExists`, double-check pending assoc requests and any stale entries.

Maya (Support): I asked the customer to run the authorization command from their acme-ops account and then we ran `associate-vpc-with-hosted-zone` in prod. Initial attempt failed with `VPCAlreadyAssociatedWithAnotherHostedZone` — turns out the prod VPC had an older private hosted zone with the same fqdn created during a migration. That older zone was empty and blocking association.

Hao (NetOps): Ah—classic split-horizon shadowing. If a VPC is associated with multiple private zones for same name, Route53 will prefer one; but the association constraints can prevent a new assoc. Steps: 1) identify the other hosted zone id (`aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --dnsname acme.internal`) 2) disassociate old/unused hosted zone from prod VPC: `aws route53 disassociate-vpc-from-hosted-zone --hosted-zone-id ZHOLD --vpc VPCRegion=us-west-2,VPCId=vpc-0f123` 3) then associate the correct hosted zone.

Maya (Support): Customer removed the stale hosted zone association and we successfully associated the correct hosted zone. After that `dig @10.0.0.2 svc.acme.internal +short` returns the expected private IPs. Customer confirmed app health checks are green. :tada:

Sam (Oncall): Nice. Two follow-ups: 1) add a note to the customer ticket about the stale hosted zone and steps taken (assoc/disassoc). 2) we should add an automation check in onboarding to detect when prod VPCs lack expected private zone associations — will file a tech debt ticket.

Hao (NetOps): Agreed — also add a doc snippet in runbook for cross-account assoc edgecases (AuthorizationAlreadyExists, VPCAlreadyAssociatedWithAnotherHostedZone).

Maya (Support): Done — ticket updated and customer happy. Closing thread. :white_check_mark:
